properties.statement: THE `contradiction` DETECTOR FIRES ON THE EDGE AND NEVER LOOKS FOR THE RESOLVING DECISION ITS OWN SKILL PROMISES — SO A CONTRADICTION CAN BE ACKNOWLEDGED OR ERASED, BUT NEVER RESOLVED. Found here on 2026-08-08 by running check-health, and only because a contradiction was deliberately recorded earlier the same session. THE DOCUMENTED CONTRACT: the served check-health skill's category table reads `contradiction` = 'two nodes joined by CONTRADICTS **with no resolving Decision**', and `suggested_fix_type` on every such issue is `generate_decision`. Both say plainly that recording a Decision is how this defect goes away. THE ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR (crates/reflow2-core/src/heal.rs, the CONTRADICTS loop): it walks every CONTRADICTS edge, skips only those carrying `alignment: supporting`, and emits an issue. IT NEVER CONSULTS ANY DECISION. Verified by execution: two TemporalFacts were joined by CONTRADICTS (a measured correction against a claim it disproved); `dec:the-stranded-server-correction-stands` was created, ACCEPTED, and edged GOVERNED_BY from BOTH endpoints, stating explicitly which clause survives and why; `detect_defects` re-run reported the identical issue id, unchanged. SO THE ONLY WAYS OUT ARE BOTH LOSSY: acknowledge_defect, which files a resolved disagreement in the same drawer as an unresolved one and so destroys the distinction the acknowledgement list exists to preserve; or delete the CONTRADICTS edge, which erases that the disagreement ever happened — and for a graph whose whole premise is that history survives, that is the worse of the two. THE IRONY IS TWENTY LINES ABOVE THE BUG, in the same loop's own comment, about the `alignment` property this detector was taught to read in July: 'the only ways out were to acknowledge a defect that is not one, or to stop recording corroboration at all. A property the detector ignores is a property that lies.' The identical sentence applies one step along: A RESOLUTION THE DETECTOR IGNORES IS A RESOLUTION THAT DOES NOTHING. The fix that was applied to `alignment` was never applied to the resolution half. FIX SHAPE: before emitting, check whether a Decision is linked to both endpoints (GOVERNED_BY from each, or a Decision naming both in an edge) and skip if so — which is exactly what `generate_decision` invites the user to build. Open question worth settling rather than assuming: whether the resolving Decision must be `accepted`, since a `proposed` one is somebody thinking out loud and should probably not silence anything. THE CLASS THIS BELONGS TO, and it is now the fourth instance this week: documented behaviour and actual behaviour disagreeing, with the documentation being the more generous of the two — alongside claim_region's schema describing the pre-shared-server architecture, cap:claim-liveness promising a `gone` that was unreachable, and check-health calling node deletion mechanical.
